TRANSCRIPT OF PROCEEDINGS
THE HON CATHERINE HOLMES AC SC, Commissioner
THE ROYAL COMMISSION INTO THE ROBODEBT SCHEME
TUESDAY, 6 DECEMBER 2022 AT 10.03 AM (AEST)
DAY 14
MR ANGUS SCOTT KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MS RENEE BERRY, Counsel Assisting
MS DOMINIQUE HOGAN-DORAN SC, for the Commonwealth
MR TRENT GLOVER, for the Commonwealth
MS PHILIPPA KELLY, for the Commonwealth
MR ALEXANDER VIAL, for the Commonwealth

COMMISSIONER: Yes. Are the appearances today any different?
MR SCOTT: May it please, Commissioner, I appear with Ms Berry today.
COMMISSIONER: And Ms Hogan-Doran.
MS HOGAN-DORAN: This morning I appear with Ms Kelly, and I think Mr Glover will be
here at lunchtime for the -
COMMISSIONER: I very much hope so.
MS HOGAN-DORAN: Yes, for the other matter.
COMMISSIONER: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Commissioner, I understand you have been provided a list of exhibits for
today's proceeding?
COMMISSIONER: Yes, I have.
MR SCOTT: I tender the documents in that list as per the numbering in that list.
COMMISSIONER: So that's 1706 - and it's all of them, is it - to 1416?
MR SCOTT: Yes, Commissioner.
COMMISSIONER: And they relate to Mr Hutson and Mr Storen?
MR SCOTT: That's so, Commissioner.
COMMISSIONER: Yes, they are exhibits with that numbering. Thank you.
MR SCOTT: Thank you, Commissioner. Commissioner, I call Craig Storen.
COMMISSIONER: Mr Storen, will you take an oath or an affirmation?
MR STOREN: An affirmation, Commissioner.
COMMISSIONER: All right. Would you just stand up for a minute and we will get that done.
<CRAIG ANDREW STOREN, AFFIRMED
<EXAMINATION BY MR SCOTT
MR SCOTT: Mr Storen, would you please tell the Commission your full name?

MR STOREN: Craig Andrew Storen.
MR SCOTT: And you received a notice to give a Statement and produce documents from the
Commission dated 20 October 2022?
MR STOREN: That's correct.
MR SCOTT: And you produced a Statement in response to that notice dated 28 October
2022?
MR STOREN: Yes, that's correct.
MR SCOTT: And you produced a Supplementary Statement in response to the notice dated
25 November 2022?
MR STOREN: Yes, that's correct.
MR SCOTT: Are the contents of those Statements true and correct to the best of your
knowledge and belief?
MR STOREN: Yes, they are.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. You commenced working in what was then called the Department
of Education in June 1985?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Initially in financial roles?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Then from about 2003 to June 2013, you were the Chief Finance Officer in that
Department?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: You then commenced in November 2014 as General Manager, Aged Care
Programs in the Department of Human Services?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then from October 2016 to 30 April 2017, you held the role of General
Manager, Strategic Information and Redesign in that Department?
MR STOREN: Yes.

MR SCOTT: And then from 1 May 2017 to 22 December 2019, you held the role of General
Manager, Customer Compliance division in that Department?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: As at 7 August 2017, you reported to Jason McNamara in that role, that last role
we just described?
MR STOREN: That was August 2017?
MR SCOTT: Yes, 7 August 2017.
MR STOREN: Yes, that's correct.
MR SCOTT: And as at 7 January 2019, you reported to Annette Musolino, who was then the
Deputy Secretary, Integrity and Information Branch of that Department?
MR STOREN: Integrity and Information Group it may have been called, but yes.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. And from 4 February 2019, you continued to report to
Ms Musolino?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. As General Manager, Compliance, in that Department, you had
some involvement in the Department's response to the Ombudsman's investigation in
April - sorry, in 2017?
MR STOREN: I didn't commence in the Customer Compliance division role until May 2017.
So the Department responded to the Ombudsman prior and produced a report in April, but I
was involved in responding to the Ombudsman's recommendations in their report, yes.
MR SCOTT: I see. So are you saying you had no involvement in the Ombudsman's
investigation in 2017, prior to the report being completed?
MR STOREN: I can't say I had no involvement whatsoever because in the Strategic
Information and Redesign role, which I was in prior to the compliance role, I did provide a
supporting data function to the whole Department in respect of all the Department's data
holdings. So I may have assisted with some data contributions for the Department's
contribution. I don't recall specifically.
MR SCOTT: Okay. Can the witness please be shown document CTH.3004.0002.7726_R,
Exhibit 1358. Can we call out, please, the email in the middle of that page. Now, Mr Storen,
can you see that purports to be an email from someone called Zhan Smith?

MR SCOTT: Dated 14 February 2017?
MR STOREN: That's correct.
MR SCOTT: To yourself?
MR STOREN: No, that's actually to Craig Kelly, who worked for me at the time, but it wasn't
directed to me.
MR SCOTT: I see. Sorry, I missed that. Now, if we just call out the first few words in that
sentence - in that email:
As per below to respond to the Ombudsman's outstanding question.
That is in the email we were just discussing?
MR STOREN: Sorry, could you repeat?
MR SCOTT: So you can see there the words in that email commence with:
Hi Craig, as per below, to respond to the Ombudsman's outstanding question.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Correct. Yes.
MR SCOTT: And in round brackets and inverted commas the question is identified:
(How many recipients, subject to OCI, have had their final outcome based on averaging.)
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT:
We have used the debt breakdown by earnings recorded data.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. And if we just call out the same email, the section headed Outcome.
It commences with:
As at 27 January 2017, 133,891 debts have been raised.

Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT:
We are unable to identify whether 1739 debts of those debts are averaged.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then the next line - sorry, the next bullet point purports to give a
percentage of debts based on averaging out of the remaining 132,152 debts. Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And the percentage is 76 per cent?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Do you see that? All right. And then if we go to the email immediately above
that. And this is an email to yourself from the other Craig, dated 14 February 2017.
MS HOGAN-DORAN: Just - it's the other way around, Commissioner. It's from Mr Storen to
Mr Kelly.
COMMISSIONER: From Mr Storen to Mr Kelly. Yes.
MR SCOTT: Sorry. I've skipped over an email. I beg your pardon. So there's actually two
emails in that section that's called out. So it should be that section there. Thank you. From
Craig Kelly to yourself, dated 14 February 2017. Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And it says:
Craig, please see our below proposed response for Jason and Alison regarding a question
from the Ombudsman. Let me know if you are okay for us to proceed and we will send
through.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Who would be Jason in this?

MR SCOTT: And who would be Alison?
MR STOREN: That would be Alison McCann.
MR SCOTT: Okay. And that - you would understand, that proposed response would be as per
that below email from Mr Smith we just discussed?
MR STOREN: It would be Ms Smith, but yes.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. That is, that as at that date, it was estimated that about 76 per cent
of debts had been raised using averaging in the Online Compliance Intervention?
MR STOREN: To the best of the ability of the data scientists that were looking at the data at
the time. It's - one of the challenges during that period was there was no field in the database
that said, "Yes, this debt was determining by averaging.” So the data scientists that were
working for me were doing the best they could with the data available to come up with that.
MR SCOTT: What methodology would they have used?
MR STOREN: My recollection is they would have looked at how the debt was determined
and looked for an even apportionment of income and made the assumption that it - an even
apportionment of income could occur from two ways: one could be averaging or
apportionment or whatever you want to call it; or a customer could actually say, "My income
was even," and therefore - and there was no field in the information data to actually sift that
through. So they basically based the data on what the numbers looked like and looking for
even number patterns to make an assumption there was averaging.
MR SCOTT: When you say, "even apportion of income", do you mean that the calculations
for the social security recipients of debts were based on an assumption that their income had
been earned in the same amount per fortnight; is that right?
MR STOREN: That's correct.
MR SCOTT: And so to come up with this figure, the data scientists in your section were
looking for calculations that used even apportionment of income?
MR STOREN: I apologise for trying to be so precise, but they were looking for patterns of
numbers that led to the calculation of the debt, yes.
COMMISSIONER: So if you got somebody with $200 every fortnight, you would assume
there had been apportionment?
MR STOREN: That's correct, Commissioner.

MR SCOTT: Can we just go to the email that comes next at the top of the page. I finally got
it right this time, I think. This is the email from yourself to Mr Kelly -
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: - in response to the previous email, dated 14 February 2017. And the words are:
Okay by me.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And may we take it that's you indicating you are okay with the proposed
response to the Ombudsman's inquiry?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. And then the next text refers to the Data61 report?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: What's the Data61 report?
MR STOREN: During that early period in February 2017 after the Robodebt issue had
become, like, prevalent and widely looked at, the data was looked at quite closely to see if we
could figure out what was going on. And it proved that the system that had been built was a
transaction system, a system whereby you actually undertake a compliance review. It didn't
have any strong, what I would call, management information behind it.
Data61 were a private company - I'm not sure who they relate to - that were data experts that
had come in. I - my recollection is they were called in by the information technology part of
the agency to try and pull the data together that was available in the transactional system to
see what the data could tell us about what was going on in terms of the numbers.
MR SCOTT: Okay.
COMMISSIONER: And there was a report done, was there?
MR STOREN: I recall a paper I've seen in the last week that's been shown to me as a
document, and it refers to a report by Data61. But that's - I don't recall a report, but I have
seen a document in the last week that refers to a report.
COMMISSIONER: Right. Thank you.
MR SCOTT: The balance of the email says that the report has:

67 per cent of customers did not respond to reviews and therefore incurred an auto-assessed
debt.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes. Yes.
MR SCOTT: And the concept of customers incurring an auto-assessed debt after not
responding to reviews, is that a reference to the process in the Online Compliance
Intervention in which customers or social security recipients would receive an initial letter
from the Department -
COMMISSIONER: Well, they would be sent it.
MR SCOTT: Sent an initial letter, I beg your pardon, indicating that there is a difference
between what had been declared to Centrelink and what had been declared to the Australian
Taxation Office in terms of income and then asked those recipients to go online and update
their details; is that right?
MR STOREN: That's my understanding of the process under OCI, yes.
MR SCOTT: And that if they didn't go online and update their details, the Online
Compliance computer program would automatically calculate their debt; correct?
MR STOREN: After the period of time, which I think the letter - initial letter advised, yes,
that's correct.
MR SCOTT: And calculate it using income averaging?
MR STOREN: That's correct.
MR SCOTT: And that's the point that you're making here, isn't it, that the data as to the
number of customers who had a debt automatically calculated was roughly lining up with
what your data scientists were saying from their inquiries about the number of debts that had
been calculated using averaging?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Now, you were aware, weren't you, that by law, social security entitlement is
calculated according to what a recipient's actual fortnightly income is? You're aware of that?
MR STOREN: So are you asking in February 2017 when I was responding to this email, was
I aware?
MR SCOTT: Yes.

MR STOREN: No.
MR SCOTT: You weren't aware that the social security law provides that -
MR STOREN: No. In February 2017, I was undertaking the role of Strategic Information and
Redesign, leading a team of data scientists, supporting the whole of the Department's data
holdings and a few other pieces. I had a supporting role of the compliance function. So, no, I
wasn't aware of the provisions of the Social Security Act at that time.
MR SCOTT: And you had - so in your role, it wasn't - sorry, I will rephrase that. It wasn't
part of your role to be informed as to how social security income recipients' entitlements were
calculated by law?
MR STOREN: Correct. It wasn't a requirement of my role in February 2017.
MR SCOTT: Okay. That document can be taken down. Can the witness please be shown
document ID CTH.1000.0011.1190_R, Exhibit 1713. Now, if we go to the email at the
bottom of the second page, please, an email from Julie Ballard. Do you see that's an email
from Julie Ballard to Michael Robinson and Jason McNamara dated 19 October 2018?
MR STOREN: Yes, I've got the email.
MR SCOTT: And you can see the words:
Hi Megan, as discussed previously, the Honourable Andrew Wilkie has made comments in
the media regarding income data matching and indicated the Ombudsman's Office were
investigating the matter.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: This is, of course, after the Ombudsman's investigation in April 2017?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Do you see that?
MR STOREN: It looks like October 2018.
MR SCOTT: Yes. It refers to previous media releases prepared in relation to this. Do you see
that, third line?
MR STOREN: Yes. Yes.

The Ombudsman's Office have just sent a letter to the Honourable...
It says "Hon", but it means Honourable:
Andrew Wilkie and his constituent Mr Dut (see attached) regarding a number of items that
were raised with the Ombudsman's Office.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then you see the next line:
To assist the Department in preparing for any potential media comments from Andrew
Wilkie, the OO...
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Which is defined in the previous paragraph as Ombudsman's Office. Do you see
that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT:
...have sent through their response to both Andrew and the constituent. Please note the
content of the letters are not to be distributed widely and there is to be no reference to the
content of the letters in any of the media points/releases. Please contact myself for further
information as required.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And you can see that Julie Ballard is the Director of the Ombudsman
Relationship and Management section. Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Do you recall Julie Ballard?
MR STOREN: The name is familiar.

MR SCOTT: Do you recall that she worked in the Department of Human Services at this
time?
MR STOREN: Sorry, could you repeat the question?
MR SCOTT: Do you recall that she worked in the Department of Human Services at this
time?
MR STOREN: No. No, I - I recall the name, and I recall it was a name around my time at
Human Services, but I - other than that, but it's evident she worked in - in the Department as a
Director.
MR SCOTT: Okay. If we go to the next email just above that and call it out. It's an email
from yourself, dated 24 October, to Julie Ballard and Michael Robinson. Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: You say:
As discussed, I have talked to our office who are looking for something tangible for the
Minister to rely on should he be pursued about the recent Wilkie tweet.
Do you see that in the first sentence?
MR STOREN: Yes. Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then you see the paragraph:
We need to give them something along the lines of...
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then there's a quote?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then the next line is:
Can we get the Ombudsman to sign up to something like that or can we go further and say
they are satisfied with our progress?
MR STOREN: Yes.

MR STOREN: No, I don't recall the email.
MR SCOTT: Okay. Do you agree that one of the things that you - having read this email now
and refreshed your memory, do you agree that one of the things that you were proposing in
this email was that the Ombudsman's agreement be sought as to the terms of the statement
from the Ombudsman's Office that could be given to the Minister?
MR STOREN: Could I just clarify - I don't think the statement is trying to quote the
Ombudsman's Office, if that's what your question was. I think the statement is trying - so I
don't have a clear recollection, but I can have a look at it and try and understand what we
were trying to do at the time. I think the statement is trying to have the Ombudsman's Office
comfortable that we were proposing to say something about their operation in a public way.
MR SCOTT: Is that - what do the words "can we get the Ombudsman to sign up to something
like that" mean?
MR STOREN: That they would not be uncomfortable if we were to say publicly - sorry, "we"
could be officials in an estimates context or "we" could mean the Minister in this context.
They would not take umbrage if we said the Commonwealth Ombudsman had looked at what
we had - as the sentence says, Commonwealth Ombudsman would not take umbrage if we
were to say at estimates or the Minister was to say they have looked at the progress we have
made on the - looking at their recommendations and trying to respond to their
recommendations, was the first point. The second point would be would they be upset if we
said they were satisfied with progress.
MR SCOTT: Okay. And when you say in the first line "something tangible for the Minister to
rely on should he be pursued about the recent Wilkie tweet", is that a reference to something
for the Minister to rely upon should he be pursued by a media inquiry about the recent Wilkie
tweet?
MR STOREN: I would be making an assumption that it would be a media inquiry, but
that's - that would be a likely scenario.
MR SCOTT: Okay. If we go to the previous page and call out the email from Ms Macleod in
the middle of the page. I'm sorry, the earlier email at the bottom of the page. Now, you can
see that's an email from Mr Robinson? Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes. Yes.
MR SCOTT: Dated 24 October 2018?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: To Louise Macleod?

MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Do you know who Louise Macleod is?
MR STOREN: Off the top of my head, I don't. But I think the previous page that was
switched up said she may have been the Deputy Commonwealth Ombudsman.
MR SCOTT: Yes. And you can see the note is:
Louise, as discussed, see below.
Referring to the earlier email from yourself to Mr Robinson:
Appreciate your advice.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. If we go to the next email up, there is Ms Macleod's response to Mr
Robinson dated 24 October 2018. And it says:
Hi Michael...
Can you see the first line?
The following has been approved by the Deputy Ombudsman for DHS to provide to the
Minister.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: So - and there is a form of words provided. Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then it ends with:
Kind regards, Louise.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: So would you agree that what Ms Macleod has authorised Mr Robinson to do is
to provide the Minister with a form of words for a statement that he can make about the
Ombudsman? Do you accept that?

MR SCOTT: Okay. And to enable him to use that statement to respond to media inquiries?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. That document can be taken down. Can the witness please be
shown document CTH.2000.0007.5540_R, Exhibit 1640. Call out the email from Media at
Wednesday, 4 April 2018. That's the words before "fine with me". It goes over the page.
Now, Mr Storen, you can see that's an email addressed to a number of persons, including
yourself, on 4 April 2018? Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then if we call out the first paragraph and the introductory words of that
email:
Hi Jason, Robert and Craig, as flagged, we have prepared a response below to an inquiry
from the Canberra Times about the Online Compliance system following the publication of
an academic article about the system.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And it refers in the next paragraph to The Guardian publishing a story about the
same article. And the third paragraph of the statement is:
We intend on contacting The Guardian about this and would like to provide them with a copy
of the response we have prepared for the Canberra Times.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And if we go to the bottom of the page, the inquiry goes over to the next page.
It opens with:
The story I'm writing is looking at a paper (attached) by Terry Carney AO...
Which you would understand to be Order of Australia?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT:

...the Emeritus Professor of Law at Sydney University about the DHS's Online Compliance
Intervention program. Professor Carney makes a number of arguments, including that legal
responsibility for obtaining all information necessary for calculating working age payment
debts based on verifiable actual fortnightly earnings rather than on the basis of assumed
averages ultimately has always rested with Centrelink.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And the next bullet point:
The OCI system should be brought into compliance with the law.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And the next bullet point:
OCI is flawed because statistical averages tell nothing about the variability or otherwise of
the underlying numbers from which averages are calculated.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Now, this is an email chain as at 4 April 2018.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And, of course, it is making a number of points about the lawfulness of using
income averaging to calculate debts to Centrelink. Can you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: As at the date of this email, were you aware that the social security law required
entitlements for social security to be calculated with actual fortnightly income?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Right. And so you, at this stage, appreciated the significance of the criticism of
using income averaging to calculate debts that's referred to in this article?
MR STOREN: I appreciated the criticism. There was a wide amount of content in the media,
including this content in the media, about averaging and the process of determining a debt.

MR SCOTT: And in the context of calculating social security entitlements; correct? You
appreciated that was of particular significance?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And the reason, of course, is that it's frequently the case that recipients of social
security have income that varies from fortnight to fortnight. You were aware of that, weren't
you?
MR STOREN: It's common, yes.
MR SCOTT: And so it's a big assumption to make that income averaging will produce an
accurate calculation of a recipient's entitlement without some evidence to confirm they have
earned income in equal amounts per fortnight?
MR STOREN: Could you repeat that? I - I don't quite agree with some of the words that you
are using in the long sentence. I agree with the thrust of what you are saying.
MR SCOTT: Can I repeat?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: It's a big assumption to make that income averaging will produce an accurate
calculation of a recipient's entitlement without some evidence to confirm they have earned
income in equal amounts per fortnight.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Do you agree with that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Yes. And you would agree that this was the fundamental - one of the
fundamental criticisms that was being made in the article from the emeritus professor that's
referred to in this media inquiry?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. Now, if we go over the page and call out the words headed Response.
The first bullet point says:
The Department of Human Services strictly adheres to legislation when conducting
compliance activities and refutes any claims to the contrary.
MR STOREN: Yes.

MR SCOTT: I should say, you understand this to be the proposed response to the inquiry?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And then the next bullet point:
The independent review by the Commonwealth Ombudsman found the Online Compliance
system meets all legislative requirements, accurately calculates debts when the required
information is entered, and debts raised are consistent with the previous investigation
processes.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. Now, would you agree with this proposition: that it was a standard
response at this time by the Department to adverse media publicity about the Robodebt
Scheme to refer to the 2017 Ombudsman report?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And in particular, to effectively rebut criticisms of the Scheme's lawfulness and
fairness?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Thank you. That document can be taken down. Can the witness please be
shown document CTH.3004.0009.0076, Exhibit 1649. Mr Storen, do you see that document
purports to be a Compliance Modernisation Program Management Dashboard?
MR STOREN: That's correct.
MR SCOTT: Would you have seen documents like this in your time in the Department of
Human Services?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And would this be right: that it - these documents were produced at regular
intervals by the Department to track the Compliance Modernisation Program's progress in
terms of meeting the Budget targets? Do you agree with that?
MR STOREN: Amongst other things. But, yes, the Budget targets were an important part of
the report.
MR SCOTT: Okay. Can we just call out the top right-hand corner section headed EIC

MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And so would you accept that FY18 would be referring to financial year 2018?
MR STOREN: It would be the 2017/2018 financial year, yes.
MR SCOTT: And TD would be "to date"?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. And you can see there is a picture that is purporting to depict
interventions completed FYTD and has a breakdown represented by the two colours, orange
and blue. Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. And one says:
Online completion, seven per cent.
Do you see that?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: And the other says:
Staff-assisted completion, 93 per cent.
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Okay. What does "online completion, seven per cent" refer to?
MR STOREN: My recollection, with a fair degree of certainty, is that would be a compliance
intervention where the customer who has received the initiation letter has logged online,
completed the intervention themselves, so apportioned their income, whatever they needed to
do, and then finalised the completion without recourse to a compliance officer.
MR SCOTT: Okay. And then - so what would, then, "staff-assisted completion" be referring
to?
MR STOREN: That would be where a - so my reading of the document is that would be
where a customer has called in to a compliance officer and the compliance officer has worked
with that customer over the phone. It may have been over several phone calls. It could have
been an exchange of data. But it basically means the compliance officer has completed the

MR SCOTT: Okay. And may we take it that what this is representing is that that second
category you have just described, 93 per cent of the interventions as at the date of this report
for financial year 2018, had been the staff-assisted kind?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Whereas only seven per cent had been the online completion kind?
MR STOREN: Yes.
MR SCOTT: Now, the Robodebt Scheme was designed, wasn't it, so that the vast majority of
recipients were supposed to complete their interventions online, wasn't it?
MR STOREN: The original Budget Measure announced by the Government prior to 2017
and the original implementation of OCI, that is correct. The intention was to be a largely
technology-driven, customer-driven process.
MR SCOTT: And that intent was fundamental to the number of assumptions as to the number
of interventions that could be completed as per the Budget Measure, wasn't it?
MR STOREN: The original costings agreed to Government prior to 2017, yes.
MR SCOTT: Right. And what this indicates is that that just was not happening as at the date
